text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Respectful, shared decision-making: take her history as given, explain each test and medicine with its reasons and alternatives, write the plan down, and check costs with her before prescribing
  • Cardiology consultation on the day of the two-week visit, with the echocardiogram, to confirm the cause of breathlessness, look for hypertensive heart disease and HFpEF and their mimics, and advise on treatment
  • Confirm the diagnosis with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring today, before the first dose; then home readings twice daily with a validated upper-arm monitor and a large cuff lent by the clinic
  • Start a two-drug combination for stage 2 hypertension: chlorthalidone 12.5 mg and amlodipine 5 mg every morning, from the morning after the ambulatory monitor is removed, as low-cost generics; target below 130/80 mmHg; less salt, using foods she already eats
  • Baseline tests: ECG, NT-proBNP, metabolic panel and magnesium, hemoglobin, TSH, hemoglobin A1c, lipids, ALT and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; echocardiogram because of raised NT-proBNP, breathlessness and suspected left ventricular hypertrophy
  • Stroke and emergency warning signs: BE FAST (balance, eyes, face, arm, speech, time to call 911), and call 911 for chest pain, severe headache with confusion or vision loss, or breathlessness at rest
  • Costs and coverage, with the clinic's community health worker: a SHINE counselor for Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program; generic medicines in 90-day fills; patient assistance for any brand-only medicine until coverage begins
  • Food: the Hunger Vital Sign at intake; help applying for SNAP through ACCESS Florida; the food pantry list
  • Heart failure treatment: dapagliflozin 10 mg daily with sick-day rules; daily weights with a written plan; metabolic panel one to two weeks after each start or dose change, then every three to six months; KCCQ-12 every three to six months
  • Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary prevention, with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks
  • Add spironolactone 12.5 mg daily for blood pressure above target and low potassium on chlorthalidone; potassium and creatinine one to two weeks later
  • Laboratory checks on the day of clinic visits where possible, and rides through the county's transportation program for people without a car when a separate trip is needed
  • Heat plan for the Florida summer: fans and cooling places, water through the day, sick-day rules for chlorthalidone, spironolactone and dapagliflozin, and the energy assistance program's cooling help

resource.title: Zora Neale Hurston synthetic care plan
resource.description: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in a 67-year-old Black woman, a writer, anthropologist and substitute teacher with a low and irregular income, in Fort Pierce, Florida. The episode covers very high blood pressure found at a visit for headaches and breathlessness, with no hypertensive emergency; confirmation by 24-hour ambulatory monitoring; ECG, echocardiogram, NT-proBNP, kidney function and urine albumin; an initial two-drug combination of a thiazide-type diuretic and a calcium channel blocker under the 1957 AHA/ACC high blood pressure guideline; an SGLT2 inhibitor and low-dose spironolactone for HFpEF under the 1954 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline; potassium and kidney monitoring on the CMID schedule, with one missed check recorded honestly; summer heat, volume depletion and sick-day rules; the stroke she is at risk of and the BE FAST warning signs; and equity in care: generic medicines in 90-day fills, patient assistance, Medicare Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program with a SHINE counselor, SNAP, energy assistance for cooling, and respect for her expertise and her own account of her life.
